section.heading: Short title

content.p: This Act may be cited as the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Legislation Amendment (Exit Arrangements) Act 2016.

section.heading: Commencement

content.p: Each provision of this Act specified in column 1 of the table commences, or is taken to have commenced, in accordance with column 2 of the table. Any other statement in column 2 has effect according to its terms.

Immediately after the revocation of a declaration under subsection 4A(1) of the Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988. However, if a declaration under that subsection is not revoked, the provisions do not commence at all.

section.heading: Application of rehabilitation provisions to former Commonwealth authorities

content.p: If:
(a) a body corporate ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the body corporate continues in existence; and
before the cessation time, an employee of the body corporate suffered an injury resulting in an incapacity for work or an impairment;
then:

(d) the definition of rehabilitation authority in subsection 4(1), and sections 36, 37, 38, 39, 41 and 41A, apply after the cessation time, in relation to the injury, as if the body corporate had not ceased to be a Commonwealth authority; and

if, after the cessation time, the employee is undertaking, or has completed, a rehabilitation program in relation to the injury—the body corporate is, for the purposes of section 40, taken to be the relevant employer of the employee.

section.heading: Application of rehabilitation provisions to successors of former Commonwealth authorities

If:
(a) a body corporate ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the body corporate ceases to exist at the cessation time; and
under a legislative instrument made by the Minister, a specified Commonwealth authority or Entity is taken to be the successor of the body corporate for the purposes of this subsection; and
before the cessation time, an employee of the body corporate suffered an injury resulting in an incapacity for work or an impairment;
then:
(e) the definition of rehabilitation authority in subsection 4(1), and sections 36, 37, 38, 39, 41 and 41A, apply after the cessation time, in relation to the injury, as if:
the employee were employed by the successor; and
the principal executive officer of the successor were the principal officer of the successor; and

if, after the cessation time, the employee is undertaking, or has completed, a rehabilitation program in relation to the injury—the successor is, for the purposes of section 40, taken to be the relevant employer of the employee.
Successor is neither a Commonwealth authority nor an Entity
If:
(a) a body corporate ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the body corporate ceases to exist at the cessation time; and

under a legislative instrument made by the Minister, a specified body, person, organisation or group of persons is taken to be the successor of the body corporate for the purposes of this subsection; and
the successor is neither a Commonwealth authority nor an Entity; and
before the cessation time, an employee of the body corporate suffered an injury resulting in an incapacity for work or an impairment;
then:
(f) the definition of rehabilitation authority in subsection 4(1), and sections 36, 37, 38, 39, 41 and 41A, apply after the cessation time, in relation to the injury, as if:
the employee were employed by the successor; and
the successor were a Commonwealth authority; and

if, after the cessation time, the employee is undertaking, or has completed, a rehabilitation program in relation to the injury—the successor is, for the purposes of section 40, taken to be the relevant employer of the employee.

section.heading: Application of rehabilitation provisions to the Australian Capital Territory if it ceases to be a Commonwealth authority

content.p: If:
(a) the Australian Capital Territory ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
before the cessation time, a person employed by the Australian Capital Territory suffered an injury resulting in an incapacity for work or an impairment;

(c) the definition of rehabilitation authority in subsection 4(1), and sections 36, 37, 38, 39, 41 and 41A, apply after the cessation time, in relation to the injury, as if the Australian Capital Territory had not ceased to be a Commonwealth authority; and

if, after the cessation time, the employee is undertaking, or has completed, a rehabilitation program in relation to the injury—the Australian Capital Territory is, for the purposes of section 40, taken to be the relevant employer of the employee.

there is an error in information given to Comcare under section 97F that affected the determination; or

section.heading: Refund of premiums to the Australian Capital Territory if it ceases to be a Commonwealth authority

content.p: If:
(a) the Australian Capital Territory ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the amount that represents so much of available scheme funds as is attributable to:
premiums paid by the Australian Capital Territory before the cessation time; and
special premiums paid by the Australian Capital Territory before the cessation time; and
interest earned on the premiums and special premiums referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii);

exceeds Comcare’s liability (if any) under this Act (including liability under actions for non-economic loss), in respect of injuries suffered before the cessation time by employees of the Australian Capital Territory;
Comcare may make a determination that an amount equal to the excess is payable to the Australian Capital Territory by way of a refund of premiums paid to Comcare by the Australian Capital Territory.
The amount is to be paid by Comcare within 28 days after the determination is made.
A determination under subsection (1) may only be made during the 7-year period beginning at the cessation time.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b):
(a) liability includes prospective liability; and
assume that Comcare’s liability is not contingent on:
the making of a claim for compensation; or
the giving of a notice under section 53.

section.heading: Refund of exit contributions to former Commonwealth authorities

content.p: If:
(a) a body corporate ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the body corporate continues in existence; and
the amount that represents so much of available scheme funds as is attributable to:
premiums paid by the body corporate before the cessation time; and
special premiums paid by the body corporate before the cessation time; and
interest earned on the premiums and special premiums referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii); and
exit contributions, or instalments of exit contributions, paid to Comcare by the body corporate after the cessation time; and
interest earned on exit contributions and instalments referred to in subparagraph (iv);
exceeds Comcare’s liability (if any) under this Act (including liability under actions for non-economic loss), in respect of injuries suffered before the cessation time:
if the body corporate did not hold a licence in force under Part VIII—by employees of the body corporate; and
if the body corporate held such a licence—by employees of the body corporate in respect of whom the body corporate was not authorised to accept liability;

Comcare may make a determination that a specified amount is payable to the body corporate by way of a refund of the whole or a part of the exit contributions, or instalments of exit contributions, paid to Comcare by the body corporate.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the specified amount must be equal to or less than the excess.
The specified amount is to be paid by Comcare within 28 days after the determination is made.
A determination under subsection (1) may only be made during the 7-year period beginning at the cessation time.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c):
(a) liability includes prospective liability; and
assume that Comcare’s liability is not contingent on:
the making of a claim for compensation; or
the giving of a notice under section 53.
Comcare may defer making a determination under subsection (1) of this section in relation to the body corporate until Comcare has made a payment to the body corporate under section 97Q.

section.heading: Refund of exit contributions to successors of former Commonwealth authorities

content.p: If:
(a) a body corporate (the first body corporate) ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the first body corporate ceases to exist at the cessation time; and
(c) under a law of the Commonwealth that was in force at the cessation time, another body corporate (the successor) becomes the successor in law of the liabilities of the first body corporate; and
the amount that represents so much of available scheme funds as is attributable to:
premiums paid by the first body corporate before the cessation time; and
special premiums paid by the first body corporate before the cessation time; and
interest earned on the premiums and special premiums referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii); and
exit contributions, or instalments of exit contributions, paid to Comcare by the successor after the cessation time; and
interest earned on exit contributions and instalments referred to in subparagraph (iv);
exceeds Comcare’s liability (if any) under this Act (including liability under actions for non-economic loss), in respect of injuries suffered before the cessation time:
if the first body corporate did not hold a licence in force under Part VIII—by employees of the first body corporate; and
if the first body corporate held such a licence—by employees of the first body corporate in respect of whom the first body corporate was not authorised to accept liability;

Comcare may make a determination that a specified amount is payable to the successor by way of a refund of the whole or a part of the exit contributions, or instalments of exit contributions, paid to Comcare by the successor.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the specified amount must be equal to or less than the excess.
The specified amount is to be paid by Comcare within 28 days after the determination is made.
A determination under subsection (1) may only be made during the 7-year period beginning at the cessation time.
(5) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c), liability means any liability, duty or obligation, whether actual, contingent or prospective.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(d):
(a) liability includes prospective liability; and
assume that Comcare’s liability is not contingent on:
the making of a claim for compensation; or
the giving of a notice under section 53.
Comcare may defer making a determination under subsection (1) of this section in relation to the successor until Comcare has made a payment to the successor under section 97QA.

section.heading: Refunds to be made from Comcare-retained funds

content.p: Comcare must make a payment under section 97Q, 97QA, 97QB, 97QBA, 97QBB or 97QBC from Comcare-retained funds.

If there is insufficient money in Comcare-retained funds to make a particular payment mentioned in subsection (1), there is payable to Comcare, out of the Consolidated Revenue Fund, which is appropriated accordingly, such an amount as is necessary to enable Comcare to make that payment.

section.heading: Remission of exit contributions payable by former Commonwealth authorities

content.p: If:
(a) a body corporate ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and
the body corporate continues in existence; and
under subsection 97HA(5), Comcare has permitted an amount of exit contribution payable by the body corporate to be paid in instalments; and
one or more of those instalments have not been paid; and
the amount that represents so much of available scheme funds as is attributable to:
premiums paid by the body corporate before the cessation time; and
special premiums paid by the body corporate before the cessation time; and
interest earned on the premiums and special premiums referred to in subparagraphs (i) and (ii); and
instalments of exit contribution paid to Comcare by the body corporate after the cessation time; and
interest earned on instalments referred to in subparagraph (iv);
exceeds Comcare’s liability (if any) under this Act (including liability under actions for non-economic loss), in respect of injuries suffered before the cessation time:
if the body corporate did not hold a licence in force under Part VIII—by employees of the body corporate; and
if the body corporate held such a licence—by employees of the body corporate in respect of whom the body corporate was not authorised to accept liability;
Comcare may remit the whole or a part of the amount of any or all of the unpaid instalments.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the total amount remitted must be equal to or less than the excess.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(e):
(a) liability includes prospective liability; and
assume that Comcare’s liability is not contingent on:
the making of a claim for compensation; or
the giving of a notice under section 53.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(e), assume that all instalments of exit contributions payable by the body corporate have been paid to Comcare.

content.p: If:
(a) a body corporate (the first body corporate) ceases to be a Commonwealth authority at a particular time (the cessation time); and

Comcare may remit the whole or a part of the amount of any or all of the unpaid instalments.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the total amount remitted must be equal to or less than the excess.
(3) For the purposes of paragraph (1)(c), liability means any liability, duty or obligation, whether actual, contingent or prospective.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(f):
(a) liability includes prospective liability; and
assume that Comcare’s liability is not contingent on:
the making of a claim for compensation; or
the giving of a notice under section 53.
For the purposes of paragraph (1)(f), assume that all instalments of exit contributions payable by the successor have been paid to Comcare.
